name: Calakmul Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Maya rainforest where jaguars, tapirs and fruit trees depend on scarce water.

tip.title: Remove the jaguar
tip.text: Lower Jaguar and watch the ripple: deer, peccaries, agoutis and monkeys lose a major predator, and vultures lose a source of carrion.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Calakmul Biosphere Reserve, Calakmul, Baird's tapir). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A common tree of the Yucatan forest whose small fruits are recorded in the diets of many birds, bats and primates.
Feeds on fruit at night, including gumbo-limbo and sapodilla, and spreads the seeds as it flies.
A browser of leaves, shoots and fruit, and a main prey of jaguars in Mexico.
An omnivorous canid that eats fruit and small mammals, and itself falls to jaguars.
Finds and eats carrion over the forest, cleaning up the kills of the big cats.
The top predator here, taking deer, peccaries, agoutis, coatis and monkeys. Calakmul and the adjoining Guatemalan forest form one of its key strongholds.
Shares the forest and many prey with the jaguar, including deer and peccaries, and also takes monkeys.
Year-round tropical light drives growth in the canopy and understory.

story: Calakmul Biosphere Reserve covers 7,231 km² of Campeche, Mexico, bordering Guatemala. With Guatemala's Maya Biosphere Reserve it forms one of the largest and least disturbed tracts of rainforest in the Americas north of Colombia. The ancient Maya city of Calakmul lies inside it.
matters: The reserve holds 5 of the 6 large cats native to Mexico, including jaguars, along with Baird's tapir and spider monkeys. Its status is critically threatened.
